title: WPMS/1080/2014 of Smt Zubeda Ahmed AND OTHERS Vs Naushad Ahmed AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1080 of 2014
Smt. Zubeda Ahmed & others ....Petitioners
Versus
Shri Naushad Ahmed & others ....Respondents
Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the respondents.
Judgment Reserved - 09.03.2017
 Date of Judgment - 10.03.2017
Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma,J.
This petition is instituted against the order
dated 17.04.2014 rendered by learned District Judge,
Dehradun in Misc. Civil Appeal No.107 of 2013 as well
as the order dated 26.08.2013 rendered by learned
Civil Judge (Jr. Div.) in Misc. Case No.20/2008 arising
out of O.S. No.416/94.
2. "Key facts" necessary for the adjudication of
this petitioner are that the respondent no.1 has
instituted a suit bearing no.416 of 1994 titled as
"Nausad Ahmed vs. Zubeda Ahmed & others". The suit
was decreed ex parte by the learned Trial Court on
16.06.1995. The decree holder instituted execution
petition bearing Execution RM 4/07.
3. Thereafter, the petitioners moved an
application under Order 9 Rule 13 to recall the ex
parte decree dated 16.06.1995. The same was
dismissed by the learned Trial Court non 26.08.2013.
Petitioners filed an appeal which was registered as
MCA No.107/2013. Learned District and Sessions
Judge, Dehradun dismissed the same on 17.04.2014.
Hence, this petition.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has
vehemently argued that the petitioners and

2
predecessors, in interest, were not served. Rule 32 of
the General Rules has not been complied with.
5. Learned counsel for the plaintiff/decree
holder has vehemently argued that the parties were
duly served. He has drawn the attention of this Court
towards the rent receipt dated 05.03.1995, wherein a
specific averment has been made that the amount has
been received without prejudice to the rights in O.S.
416 of 1994.
6. I have heard learned counsel for both the
parties and gone through the order dated 26.08.2013
and judgment dated 17.04.2014 carefully.
7. The application was filed for setting aside
the ex parte decree. It was dismissed as noticed
hereinabove.
8. It cannot be believed that the parties did not
know about the pendency of the Original Suit
No.416/94 in view of the receipt dated 05.03.1995.
9. The restoration application has been filed by
the petitioners after 13 years of passing of ex parte
decree dated 16.06.1995. It is evident from the record
that the summons were sent through registered post
and the parties have received the same as per paper
nos.8A and 9A(1). The summons were also served
upon the parties personally including their successors
and they have not denied their signatures on the
summons and registered AD cover specifically.
10. In AIR 1988 Karnataka 221, in the case of
"Manchalal & another vs. Manikchand & others", their
Lordships have held that endorsement of serving
officer on summons to the effect that summons were

3
received by defendant personally will amount to valid
service. Their Lordships have held as under:-
"11. The cause-title of the plaint discloses the
address of the both the defendants as residing at No. 83,
Rangaswamy Temple Street, Bangalore-2. There is no
contention in the Written Statement making out that the
defendants have been residing at some other address.
That case of defendants has come out, for the first time
when Defendant I examined himself on 21-9-1976 as
D.W. 2. The fact that Exhibit P-8 has been received by
Defendant 2 personally, as per, the endorsement of the
Serving Officer on Exhibit P-8 and the proof of Exhibit
P-8(a) on Exhibit P-8 leads to the conclusion that the
said summons had been served on Defendant 2 at the
address shown therein and which is the address found
in the cause-title. There is no evidence produced by the
defendants to the effect that Exhibit P-8 was served on
Defendant 2 in some other place. Therefore, an
argument, of possibility of Exhibit P-8 having been
served on Defendant 2 at a place other than the address
shown therein cannot be entertained. Hence, we hold
that the evidence of Defendant 1 that he and Defendant
2 have been residing in an address other than one
described in the cause-title cannot be relied upon as it
is patently an after thought."
11. In AIR 1996 Calcutta 242, in the case of
"United Commercial Bank vs. Mrs. Raka Sen (Nandi)",
learned Single Judge has held that the summons
served by way of registered post with
acknowledgement due amounts to effective service.
Learned Single Judge has held as under:-
"10. Looking at the reasonings given in the
aforesaid two judgments and in view of the fact that
there is no denial of the signature on oath after
inspection and in view of the fact that the petitioner's
own reading of the signature and submission in Court
that the signature is different and not of Kartick
Roychowdhury as alleged in the petition, I am satisfied
that there is no rebuttal of the service by registered post
and in the fact of the case the Court rightly proceeded
on the basis of the presumption that arises in respect
of--service by registered post. It is to be remembered
that the acknowledgement purports to be signed on
behalf of the petitioner herself and there is no denial
that the above address was not proper and it is admitted

4
that she resides at and carries on business at the
addressed given.
11. I am also impressed by the fact, that in this case the
service of the writ of summons was elected through the
appropriate Court, i.e. Alipore Court. The bailiffs
endorsement with regard to the service is there and it
has, inter alia, been stated in the bailiffs endorsement
time the bailiff went to the premises to serve the writ of
summons together with copy of the plant on 5th
December, 1984 at about 8 a.m. and the petitioner after
going through the contents of the same refused to sign
any acknowledgement of the receipt of the same. It has
further been stated by bailiff in his report that thereafter
the bailiff affixed the copies of the writ of summons and
the copy of the plaint at the outer door of the petitioner's
promises. Here also the denial of the petitioner seems to
be very cryptic. She says that it no point of time the
petitioner received the writ of summons or copy of the
plaint from the bailiff of this Hon'ble Court First of all
the bailiff was not of this Hon'ble Court and secondly
she does not deny that the bailiff came and saw her and
that she refused to receive the summons and the plaint
nor does she say that there was no occasion for the
bailiff to affix the copy of summons and the plaint at the
outer door of the petitioner's premises. The petitioner
has not even cared to see or to go through the contents
of the mode of service by the bailiff. I have no reasons
even to disbelieve the declaration made by the process
server of the Alipore Court. It to be noted that I asked
the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner
whether his client was willing to furnish security of a
sum which should not be less than Rs. 2 lakhs and it
was submitted on behalf of the petitioner that she is not
in a position to furnish any security whatsoever.
However, if any order is made as to costs of the suit
then she will comply with the same.
12. Looking at the facts of the case. I am not satisfied
with the case made out by the petitioner and I am not
satisfied that there was no due or proper service on the
petitioner in accordance with law."
12. In 2008 (1) SCC 358, in the case of
"Mahabir Singh vs. Subhash & others", their Lordships
have held that period of limitation to be reckoned from
the date of knowledge of passing of the ex parte decree
and hence application filed after 1 1⁄2 years was barred
by limitation. Their Lordships have held as under:-
"6. The approach of the High Court, in our
opinion, was not correct. There exists a presumption
that the official act was been done in ordinary course of
business. Admittedly, an ex parte decree was passed.
Defendant for getting it set aside was required to
establish that either no summons was served on him or
he had sufficient cause for remaining absent on the date
fixed for hearing the suit ex parte.

5
7. Article 123 of the Limitation Act, 1963 provides for 30
days time for filing such an application. The said
provision reads thus:
"Description of
application
Period of
limitation
Time from which period
begins to run
123. To set aside a decree
passed ex parte or to
rehear an appeal
decreed or heard ex
parte.
Thirty
days.
The date of the decree or
where the summons or
notice was not duly
served, when the
applicant had knowledge
of the decree."
Explanation.- For the
purpose of this
article, substituted
service under Rule 20
of Order 5 of the Code
of Civil Procedure,
1908 (5 of 1908) shall
not be deemed to be
due service.

8. Thus, even assuming for the sake of argument that
no proper step was taken by the appellant herein for
service of summons upon the respondent and/or the
service of summons was irregular, evidently, it was for
the defendant-respondent to establish as to when he
came to know about the passing of the ex parte decree.
Even in his cross-examination, the first respondent has
categorically admitted that he had approached the
appellant herein for not giving effect thereto one and
half year prior to filing of the application, and, thus, he
must be deemed to have knowledge about passing of the
said ex parte decree. The period of limitation would,
thus, be reckoned from that day. As the application
under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure
was filed one and a half year after the first respondent
came to know about passing of the ex parte decree in
the suit, the said application evidently was barred by
limitation.
9. In terms of Section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1963, no
court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or
application if the same has been filed after expiry of the
period of limitation. The High Court could not have
ignored the said jurisdictional fact."
13. Petitioners have not even given the exact
date of knowledge of the decree. It is evident that the
petitioners have filed the application for setting aside
the ex parte decree only when the decree holders have
instituted the execution petition against them.
Respondent no.1 has duly proved that the summons
were duly served upon the successors in interest of the

6
petitioners. Petitioners have also not assigned any
cogent or convincing reasons for condonation of delay
in filing the application for setting aside the ex parte
decree dated 16.06.1995.
14. In the present case, the process server has
filed the affidavit to the effect that he has served the
summons personally on the parties and there is
endorsement below the same by a person that he has
sworn the affidavit in his presence.
15. The petitioners all throughout knew about
the pendency of the suit and despite that they did not
participate in the proceedings. Moreover, petitioners
were not even diligent enough to move an application
under Section 5 of the Limitation Act. Both the courts
below have recorded the concurrent findings. The
concurrent findings cannot be set aside in this
jurisdiction.
16. Learned counsel for the petitioners has
drawn the attention of this Court towards page no.28
of the paper book dated 07.11.1994. It is not the copy
of summons. Rather, this was the notice served upon
the successors in interest of the petitioners to vacate
the premises. Thereafter, the suit was instituted on
11.11.1994.
17. Accordingly, there is no merit and in this
petition and the same is hereby dismissed.
Date: 10.03.2017 (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
NISHANT
